rationale: Recurring verb of diagnostic inspection throughout this kephalaion (lines 9, 11, 15, 17, 20, 22, 26). Used both of the wise physician's examination of the sick man and of the apostle's examination of the cross of light. Likely Lyc. reflex of a verb of close inspection (possibly cognate with Sah. ⲥⲱⲙ 'investigate' or ϫⲱⲱⲙⲉ 'look-up'). The pairing ⲍⲱⲙ ⲁⲭⲱϩ ('examine him') vs. ⲉⲓⲡⲉ ⲛⲉϩ ('declare to him') gives the diagnostic-prescriptive sequence.

proposed_english: the cheering of his heart / rallying of heart
rationale: Distinct from accumulated ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ 'purpose of heart' — here ⲧⲱⲕ functions in the medical-affective register: encouragement, kindling-of-heart given by the physician. Lyc. ⲧⲱⲕ may render Sah. ⲧⲱⲕ 'kindle, encourage' (Crum).
Lyc. ⲟⲩⲭⲉⲓⲧⲉ = Sah. ⲟⲩϫⲁⲓ 'health, salvation, well-being.' Medical-soteriological register: the physician gives ⲡⲟⲩⲭⲉⲓⲧⲉ alongside therapy. The Lyc. ⲭ for ϫ is regular.

Negative-affective noun paired with ⲃⲗⲕⲉ 'anger' (line 27) and used twice on this page (lines 17, 27) in the explicit doublet construction 'in wrath and anger.' Likely Lyc. reflex of ⲛⲟⲩϭⲥ̄ 'wrath' or related anger-stem. Confidence moderate.

proposed_english: the suffering one / the afflicted one
rationale: Substantival qualitative ⲡⲉⲧ- + ϩⲁⲭ (Lyc. for ϩⲱϫ 'be afflicted, oppressed'?). Modifier of ⲑⲉⲣⲁⲡⲉⲓⲁ 'therapy' — the therapy 'of the suffering one.' Fits the medical context.

Verb in the construction ⲡϣⲱⲛⲉ ⲉⲧⲁϩⲛⲉⲍⲥⲉ ⲁⲡⲁϩ 'the sickness which has befallen him' (line 5). Possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ 'wake' in transferred sense 'come upon, befall' — paralleling Sah. ϣⲱⲡⲉ ⲉϫⲛ̄. Confidence moderate.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲉϫⲛ̄ 'upon' — used in line 9 of the diagnostic 'examination of that which is upon his members.' The Lyc. ⲁⲭⲛ̄ for ⲉϫⲛ̄ shows ⲭ for ϫ and ⲁ for ⲉ — both regular. Distinct from ⲁϫⲛ̄ 'without.'

proposed_english: to remove from / to expel from
rationale: Lyc. verb of removal/expulsion. ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲟ likely related to ⲧⲟⲩⲱ/ⲧⲟⲩⲟ 'send forth, expel' (parallel to but distinct from accumulated ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise'). With ⲁⲡⲁϩ 'from him' = 'remove from him.' Medical register: physician removes sickness.

Substantival noun in line 29 with reduplicative continuation ⲍϣ ⲁⲛ in line 30. Possibly cognate with ⲍⲱϣ 'afflict' attested on the same page (ⲁⲕⲍⲉϣⲍⲱϣϩ line 30). Names the labor of revealing the soul's mysteries on the cross of light.

proposed_english: the other face / the other aspect
rationale: ⲍⲟ = Lyc. ϩⲟ 'face' (in glossary as ⲡⲍⲟ). In Mani's paraphrase of Matt 6:21 (line 31-32), the heart-treasure pair is reformulated with 'the other face' — likely the typological-reciprocal aspect of the heart in correspondential reading. Alternative 'the other treasure' (ⲍⲟ for Sah. ⲁϩⲟ) is also possible. Confidence low.
